# Use TypeScript for the app and server

> **Decision:** Use TypeScript everywhere. **Because** the team already writes it. **Accepted cost:** a build step and type errors to fix before shipping. **Revisit if** the team moves to another language.

## Context and Problem Statement
Which language should fieldnotes be written in?

## Decision Drivers
- The team writes TypeScript every day (your answer)
- Express starter (seen in package.json)

## Considered Options
1. TypeScript
2. JavaScript

## Decision Outcome
Chosen: TypeScript, because the team already writes it and errors show up before users see them.

### Consequences
- Good, because type errors show up before users see them.
- Bad, because there is a build step to keep working.

## More Information
- Confidence: high; every driver is seen in the repo or answered.

decisions.title: Choose persistence for users and projects
decisions.scope: What database/storage holds users and projects, and where it runs (file, managed DB, etc). Everything else depends on this.
decisions.why: Moving user data later requires migration and downtime; hosting choice also locks cost and backup model.

decisions.title: Choose authentication mechanism
decisions.scope: How users sign up and log in (password, magic link, OAuth provider), and password storage rules. Not session cookie format.
decisions.default: Email + password with secure hashing, add OAuth later
decisions.why: Auth UX affects signup friction and recovery; switching methods forces all users to re-authenticate.

decisions.title: Define saved project model and ownership
decisions.scope: What a project contains, ownership vs sharing, limits per user, versioning/history. Not how it's stored.
decisions.default: Projects owned by one user, private, JSON blob + metadata, limit 100 per user
decisions.why: Defines API shape and access checks; changing from private to shared later rewrites all permission logic.

decisions.title: Choose session handling and security
decisions.scope: How login persists across requests (cookies vs tokens), expiry, refresh, and CSRF/XSS protections.
decisions.default: HttpOnly secure cookie sessions with 30d expiry
decisions.why: Impacts security and mobile/web compatibility, but can be swapped with a careful migration.

decisions.title: Decide account deletion and data retention policy
decisions.scope: What delete does, grace period, hard delete vs anonymize, and GDPR/export handling.
decisions.default: Soft delete 30 days then hard delete, with export on request
decisions.why: Legal commitment to users; changing it later risks accidental data loss or non-compliance.
decisions.budget_note: over the 3-question budget; default recorded for review

options.name: One owner, private, current version only, with per-user limit
options.analogy: Like a private notebook on your shelf - only you have the key, you only see the last page you wrote, and you have a limit on how many notebooks fit.
